column1: # Inputs of the table rights-checks.tsv: the generator builds tests from them, check_spec checks every input against the table.
# case: only — row n is violated first and no later evaluable row is violated; pair — row n is violated first and the nearest later evaluable row too;
# nopair — row n has no pair, body says why; pass — no row is violated (n is 0). Evaluable — whose when evaluates on this input without a CEL error.
# Only a row after which no row of this input is evaluable, or the last row of its route, has no pair.

# body — the request object of the table (the query of GET /v1/get already in form; rights — a rights file is loaded). Parameter values and rights are the probes' own, small ones (the norm has only the #lim names of the table):

column4: row 2 needs a peer of -api, row 1 a socket or a writer: they never hold together, and the later rows read the effective role, which row 1 already refused
row 3 needs a trusted peer of the group, row 2 an untrusted one: they never hold together
row 3 needs the forwarded role admin, row 4 an effective role that is not admin: they never hold together
